chunks: He said: And Hanan narrated to me from Abu Abdur-Rahman al-Masudi, who said: Minhal ibn Amr narrated to us from Abu Abdillah al-Nu'man from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Master of the Affair [the Imam] will be imprisoned for a time, and die for a time, and flee [escape] for a time.

key_terms.حِينًا: For a time / at a time.
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Affair, a title for the Imam, specifically referring to Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.) in the context of the Occultation.

ai.seo_question: What are the three states of the Imam during the Major Occultation according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) outlines the dynamic states of the Master of the Affair during the Major Occultation, emphasizing that his concealment involves alternating periods of imprisonment, death (or apparent death), and flight. This variability refutes the static notion of the Waqifiya, illustrating that the Imam's hiddenness is a transitional phase of divine testing rather than a permanent, unchanging state of absence.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 54 - Narrated to me Hanan from Abu Abdur Rahman Masudi that he said: Narrated to us: Minhal bin Amr from Abu Abdullah Noman from Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s) that he said:
The Master of the affair [Imamate] would be imprisoned once and also die at a time and flee [escape from prison].
